issue.title: Codex's own /images/generations relay isn't written to the Requests log or Routing
issue.body:
Found while checking an X report (aidavi_, Codex imagegen 502/EOF on Plus, 2026-11-06). The report couldn't be reproduced: Plus and Pro accounts and real codex exec all generated images through magpie at 4ef47b3f4.

The gap: when Codex picks its own OpenAI model, its `backend-api/codex/images/generations` call passes through magpie but isn't recorded. Only `/responses` is written to the Requests log and Routing page. So when a user reports an imagegen failure, their magpie can't show what failed or whose connection closed.

A second, smaller mismatch: this relay waits up to 10 minutes for response headers. magpie's own image path uses Settings → Image generation timeout instead.

Expected: the relay writes a Requests row (status, duration, error) like /responses does.

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5526-codex-image-relay-records), commit [3478b2afa](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/3478b2afa41fba34a3443dd30b2d8266cf8dcc80), based on `ed0ab567`.

Codex's native `backend-api/codex/images/generations` relay now writes a Routing trace and a linked Requests row with status, duration and a bounded error, like `/responses` does, and its upstream call follows the configured image-generation timeout instead of a fixed one. The response is still forwarded as it arrives; records carry no image bytes, prompt, credential or upstream refusal body. If a failure happens after the headers are sent, the client keeps the status it received and the record shows the failure.

A real local fake-upstream regression showed no records and no deadline on the base. The patch passes related gateway tests under `-race -shuffle=on`: success, upstream refusal, key refusal, connection close, a virtual-clock timeout with a transport arrival barrier, and persisted-privacy assertions; gateway vet and the full offline `nogui` build pass.

No real vendor, full suite or cross-platform run; a cancel after the response headers was not exercised separately. AI-assisted implementation and review.
